einzeiler: James Talarico on his high-stakes Texas Senate race, billionaires, and the rage economy.
kurzfassung: James Talarico discusses his competitive Senate campaign in Texas, where he faces heavy opposition and massive funding from Republicans. He explains his shift from viewing politics through a left-right lens to focusing on a top-down dynamic driven by corporate influence. Talarico also addresses his personal attacks, his background as a public school teacher, and his appeal to moderate and Republican voters.
stichpunkte: James Talarico runs as the Democratic Senate nominee in Texas against Ken Paxton, facing significant financial backing from national Republican figures and billionaires.
Talarico describes modern political discourse as a rage economy fueled by online platforms and extreme rhetoric.
His political awakening stemmed from his time as a public school teacher in San Antonio during major state education budget cuts.
He criticizes the influence of big money in politics, advocating for bans on corporate PACs, super PACs, and congressional stock trading.
Talarico proposes short-term solutions like suspending federal gas and diesel taxes to address the affordability crisis.
He supports abolishing the filibuster to allow the political majority to govern and enact meaningful reform.
Talarico emphasizes his Christian faith as a motivation for public service, arguing that faith and politics should not be artificially separated.

beschreibung:
James Talarico is asking Texas to do something it hasn’t done in nearly 40 years: Elect a Democrat to the U.S. Senate. It won’t be easy. It will take a vast coalition of Democrats, independents and Republicans in a bright red state that President Trump won by about 14 percentage points in 2024 — and where Republicans have plowed hundreds of millions of dollars into beating Mr. Talarico. And yet, poll after poll shows that Mr. Talarico could pull it off and defeat his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general and a Trump ally.
On Monday, nearly two weeks before Election Day, Michael Barbaro spoke with Mr. Talarico about the kind of race he’s running, why it has succeeded so far in appealing to Republicans and what he wants Democrats to do if they flip control of the Senate on Nov. 3.
Guest: James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Texas.
